title: SQL tracking store bulk upserts: dedupe rows by conflict key before calling _bulk_upsert, because PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT rejects duplicates
answers: Adding a bulk write or upsert for many rows in the SQL tracking store fails on PostgreSQL with 'cannot affect row a second time'
Two different tasks on the same path: a new bulk-upserted entity that receives repeated keys in one request should keep the last value on every backend
Where is the batched upsert helper used and how does it pick the SQL for each database?
body:
Path: Bulk writes of child rows in the SQL tracking store (for example logged model tags via SqlAlchemyStore.set_logged_model_tags, and span rows) go through the _bulk_upsert helper, which emits one native dialect upsert per batch of 100 rows on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL and a session.merge fallback elsewhere.
Rule: Before passing rows to _bulk_upsert, collapse them to one row per conflict key (for example {tag.key: tag.value for tag in tags}, last occurrence wins). The dedupe is done in the caller, not in the helper. Keeping last-wins matches the old session.merge loop, so every dialect returns the same stored value.
Symptom: A request that repeated a key within a single bulk write succeeded on SQLite and MySQL but failed on PostgreSQL with CardinalityViolation, because ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE cannot touch the same row twice in one statement.
Constraints: Needed only when the conflict key can repeat inside one call. Not needed for merge-loop-only dialects, but the dedupe is harmless there. Verify a new caller with a repeated-key test, since the default CI suite runs the store tests against PostgreSQL and MySQL.
Applies: Any new or changed caller of _bulk_upsert in mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py.
applies: Callers of the SQL tracking store bulk upsert helper; not the file store or artifact paths.
says: Saving multiple model tags with duplicate keys fails when using a Postgres database.
Updating model tags in bulk should keep the latest value if keys repeat.
Batch logging traces crashes when identical keys appear multiple times in one request.
Adding tags with duplicate names works on MySQL but crashes on Postgres.
search: Callers of _bulk_upsert in mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py must collapse child rows to one row per conflict key, keeping the last occurrence, before calling the helper. This caller-side deduplication prevents CardinalityViolation errors on PostgreSQL when ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE touches the same row twice in one batch, ensuring consistent last-wins behavior across SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL backends. The rule applies to new or modified callers of _bulk_upsert in mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py where conflict keys can repeat in a single request, such as set_logged_model_tags and span writes, but is not needed for file store, artifact paths, or merge-loop-only dialects.
